items.q: A boy has recurrent knee haemarthroses, prolonged APTT, normal PT and normal platelets. Factor VIII is absent. Diagnosis?
items.exp: Haemophilia A (factor VIII deficiency) causes X linked deep joint bleeding with isolated APTT prolongation. Haemophilia B is clinically identical but lacks factor IX, requiring assay separation.
r: Incorrect. That lacks factor IX, not VIII.
Correct. Factor VIII absence means haemophilia A.
Incorrect. Type 3 vWD adds mucocutaneous bleeding and adhesion failure.
Incorrect. Factor XIII deficiency shows normal screening with clot instability.
items.kp: Joint bleeds plus isolated APTT: assay VIII then IX.

items.q: Christmas disease is another name for which deficiency?
items.exp: Haemophilia B, factor IX deficiency, is Christmas disease after an early described patient. It is indistinguishable clinically from haemophilia A without factor assays.
r: Incorrect. Factor VIII deficiency is haemophilia A.
Correct. Christmas disease is factor IX deficiency.
Incorrect. Factor XI deficiency is haemophilia C with milder bleeding.
Incorrect. Factor VII deficiency prolongs PT instead.

items.q: Commonest inherited bleeding disorder with mucocutaneous bleeding and menorrhagia is what?
items.exp: Von Willebrand disease affects up to one percent with mucosal bleeding, easy bruising and heavy periods, from defective platelet adhesion and factor VIII carriage.
r: Incorrect. Haemophilia causes deep bleeding in males mainly.
Correct. Von Willebrand disease is commonest.
Incorrect. Bernard Soulier is a rare platelet receptor defect with giant platelets.
Incorrect. Glanzmann disease is a rare aggregation defect.
items.kp: Mucocutaneous bleeding default answer is von Willebrand disease.

items.q: Mild type 1 von Willebrand disease responds to desmopressin by which mechanism?
o: Releasing stored von Willebrand factor and factor VIII from endothelium
items.exp: Desmopressin triggers endothelial release of stored von Willebrand factor (with factor VIII), transiently correcting mild type 1 disease. It fails in type 3 where stores are absent.
r: Incorrect. Concentrates, not desmopressin, supply the factor.
Correct. It releases endothelial stores.
Incorrect. Antifibrinolytics are separate adjuncts.
Incorrect. Platelet numbers do not rise from this drug.
items.kp: Desmopressin empties endothelial stores; absent stores cannot respond.

items.q: DIC laboratory pattern is which combination?
o: High platelets, high fibrinogen, low D dimer
Low platelets, low fibrinogen, very high D dimer, prolonged times
items.exp: Consumption lowers platelets and fibrinogen, prolongs PT and APTT, while fibrin breakdown floods D dimer upward. Schistocytes appear from microvascular fibrin shearing red cells.
r: Incorrect. Consumption lowers, not raises, platelets and fibrinogen.
Correct. Low platelets and fibrinogen with high D dimer define DIC.
Incorrect. DIC prolongs both screening times.
Incorrect. DIC always disturbs the laboratory panel.
items.kp: DIC consumes platelets and fibrinogen while D dimer explodes.

items.q: Vitamin K deficiency lowers which factor group?
o: Factors II, VII, IX, X and proteins C and S
items.exp: Vitamin K gamma carboxylates factors II, VII, IX, X and anticoagulant proteins C and S, so deficiency and warfarin lower all of them. Factor VII falls first with shortest half life.
r: Incorrect. V and VIII are not vitamin K dependent.
Correct. II, VII, IX, X plus C and S need vitamin K.
Incorrect. XIII is vitamin K independent.
Incorrect. Fibrinogen synthesis does not need vitamin K.
items.kp: Vitamin K factors: two, seven, nine, ten.

items.q: Umbilical stump bleeding with normal PT, APTT, platelets and bleeding time suggests which deficiency?
items.exp: Factor XIII cross links fibrin after screening tests complete, so its deficiency shows normal routine labs with delayed umbilical and wound bleeding and poor clot stability.
r: Incorrect. VIII deficiency prolongs APTT.
Correct. XIII deficiency hides behind normal screens.
Incorrect. vWD prolongs bleeding time patterns.
Incorrect. VII deficiency prolongs PT.
items.kp: Normal screens plus stump bleeding means factor XIII.

items.q: An elderly man develops spontaneous bruising and prolonged APTT from acquired factor VIII inhibitor. This mimics which disease?
items.exp: Acquired haemophilia from autoantibodies against factor VIII causes soft tissue bleeding in older adults without prior history or joint predominance. Mixing studies fail to correct.
r: Correct. Acquired factor VIII inhibitor mimics haemophilia A.
Incorrect. Platelet counts remain normal in this disorder.
Incorrect. DIC consumes multiple factors with thrombocytopenia.
Incorrect. Liver failure prolongs PT prominently too.
items.kp: New bleeding in the elderly with isolated APTT: hunt an inhibitor.

items.q: Giant platelets with defective adhesion from GPIb deficiency describe which syndrome?
items.exp: Bernard Soulier syndrome lacks platelet GPIb von Willebrand receptor, causing giant platelets, thrombocytopenia and adhesion failure. Glanzmann disease instead lacks GPIIb IIIa aggregation.
r: Incorrect. Glanzmann lacks aggregation receptor with normal sized platelets.
Correct. GPIb loss with giant platelets is Bernard Soulier.
Incorrect. Grey platelet lacks alpha granules with different morphology.
Incorrect. May Hegglin has inclusions with milder bleeding.
items.kp: Giant platelets plus adhesion failure equals Bernard Soulier.

items.q: In DIC management, which principle outranks platelet and plasma transfusion?
o: Treating the underlying trigger such as sepsis or obstetric cause
items.exp: DIC is driven by its trigger, so source control (treating sepsis, delivering in obstetric catastrophe, ATRA in promyelocytic leukaemia) is primary. Products support bleeding patients, not numbers alone.
r: Incorrect. Heparin suits selected chronic thrombotic DIC only.
Correct. Treat the trigger first in DIC.
Incorrect. Bleeding patients need product support.
Incorrect. Antifibrinolytics can worsen thrombosis in DIC.
items.kp: No trigger control, no DIC control. Treat the cause.
